definitions.explanation: A piece of cloth or knitted fabric worn around the neck for warmth. A slightly old-fashioned or literary word; マフラー is more common in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}いので{襟巻|えりま}きを{巻|ま}いた。
examples.english: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}が{毛糸|けいと}の{襟巻|えりま}きを{編|あ}んでくれた。
examples.english: My grandmother knitted a woolen scarf for me.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{襟巻|えりま}きをした{雪|ゆき}だるまが{庭|にわ}に{立|た}っていた。
examples.english: A snowman wearing a red scarf was standing in the yard.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {襟|えり} (collar/neck) and {巻|ま}き (wrapping). Considered slightly old-fashioned — younger speakers tend to use マフラー instead. Still common in literature, descriptions of traditional clothing, and among older speakers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {襟巻|えりま}きを{巻|ま}く (to wrap a scarf around one's neck)
- {襟巻|えりま}きを{外|はず}す (to take off a scarf)
- {毛皮|けがわ}の{襟巻|えりま}き (a fur stole)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マフラー: muffler, scarf — the modern, everyday word
- ストール: stole — a wider, fashion-oriented wrap for the shoulders
